symptom: Published OData entity with no KEY, or with a single KEY on an attribute without a unique rule, passes `mxcli check` and `exec`; `mx check` reports CE6585 "Published entity 'ModA.EntA' must have a key defined." / CE6624 "Add a unique validation rule to attribute 'Name' of entity 'ModA.EntA' to be able to use it as the key."
cause: No check-time rule existed. The KEY requirement was known (MDL-ODATA02's suggestion quotes CE6585, the quick reference names CE6624) but only as prose
file: `mdl/executor/validate_odata_keys.go` (new `ValidateODataKeys`, MDL-ODATA08/09, wired in `validate_program.go` so exec's preflight refuses too); `validate_import_mapping_find.go` `entityFacts` gains `view` + `uniqueAttrs` (script first, project second)
insight: **Measure the boundary before writing the predicate: the obvious rule ('every KEY attribute must be unique') is a false refusal.** mx 11.6.6, one service per case in one app: no KEY -> CE6585 for persistent, non-persistent AND view entities, also `expose (*)` and no expose clause; single KEY on a persistable entity without a unique VALIDATION RULE -> CE6624 on OData3 and OData4 alike, and `not null` or an index does not count; composite KEY with no unique rule -> clean (OData4; OData3 is CE7238, a different rule); single KEY on a non-persistent or view entity -> clean. **A CE1613 in the same app hid every key error**: an inherited key attribute is written qualified with the child entity (CE1613), and with it present mxbuild reported none of the CE6585s the other services had, so measure each case without unrelated errors in the app. The rule stays silent on inherited attributes rather than guess. Two committed bug-tests (595 `expose (*)`, 1357's keyless intermediate statement) were themselves CE6585 and had to be keyed. Guard `TestODataKeyRules_*` (revert control: 9 script cases + the project case fail); repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/1426-odata-key-requires-unique-rule.fail.mdl`
